[737] Self-Defense as a Universal Defense Policy All sovereign states prioritize ensuring national security and protecting and promoting national interests

[738] Self-Defense is the pursuit of the ability to realize these goals

[739] Therefore, all countries advocate self-defense, which aims to protect themselves from various security threats, as their basic national defense policy

[740] For example, countries that maintain alliances or close security cooperation with the United States, such as Japan, Taiwan, Australia, and Canada, also pursue self-reliant national defense as the fundamental direction of their national defense policies, explicitly stating this in public documents such as the Defense White Paper

[741] In other words, self-reliant national defense is a universal defense policy pursued by all nations, and our self-reliant national defense is also part of our national will to become an active party capable of defending national sovereignty through our own power

[742] Utilizing Inter-State Cooperation as a Primary Security Tool Modern self-reliant national defense refers to cooperative self-reliant national defense that utilizes inter-state cooperation as a primary security tool

[743] The self-reliant national defense we pursue also encompasses the acquisition of self-defense capabilities and the development of security cooperation

[744] In today's environment of heightened inter-state cooperation and interdependence, national security cannot be fully guaranteed solely through domestic capabilities

[745] Even the United States, the sole superpower, actively utilizes alliances and security cooperation relationships with various countries

[746] Permanently neutral countries like Switzerland and Austria also maintain close cooperative relationships with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) under the banner of self-reliant defense

[747] COMPONE ENT COMMAN Military Command Section 1: Concept and Direction of Cooperative Self-Reliant Defense and are developing these relationships

[748] Thus, in modern times, in addition to efforts to secure self-defense capabilities, a multi-faceted defense posture is being established through various forms of security cooperation

[749] Maintaining and Developing a Robust ROK-US Alliance Considering Korea's geostrategic circumstances, history teaches us that an "alliance strategy" is inevitable

[750] Given the uncertain security situation in Northeast Asia and the surrounding major powers, our independent capabilities alone are severely limited in ensuring national security and protecting national interests

[751] In this regard, the United States has been Korea's most important partner in politics, diplomacy, economics, and technological cooperation for the past 50 years

[752] Building on the foundation of the ROK-US alliance, we have pursued shared security interests while sharing the values of "free democracy" and "market economy

[753] Maintaining and developing the alliance with the United States will continue to be a key security element for the establishment of a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula, the unification process, and Korea's survival and prosperity after unification

[754] Therefore, cooperative self-reliant defense is a process of strengthening the ROK-US alliance on the foundation of self-defense capabilities and, based on this, strengthening security cooperation with neighboring countries

[755] This process enhances Korea's absolute security capabilities and enhances stability

[756] Chapter 4: Current Status and Challenges of Our National Defense ▲ Goals and Directions The Ministry of National Defense established the "Cooperative Self-Reliant Defense Promotion Plan" with the goal of "building a foundation for self-reliant national defense within the Roh Moo-hyun administration's term," in accordance with President Roh Moo-hyun's strategic guidelines

[757] It reported this plan to the President on November

[758] Meanwhile, the Ministry of National Defense established the basic concept and plan for promoting "self-reliant national defense" in May and July

[759] This "Cooperative Self-Reliant Defense Promotion Plan" supplements and develops this existing plan in response to changes in national defense conditions, such as the deployment of US Forces Korea to Iraq and the implementation of the reduction plan in May and June

[760] The "Cooperative Self-Reliant Defense Promotion Plan" is broadly divided into three areas: "Future-Oriented Development of the ROK-US Alliance," "Early Expansion of War Deterrence Capabilities," and "Military Structure Reorganization and Defense Reform

[761] It also outlines the defense budget requirements to achieve these objectives

[762] a. Future-Oriented Development of the ROK-US Alliance "Future-Oriented Development of the ROK-US Alliance" refers to the advancement of the ROK-US Alliance, which has served as the fundamental pillar of our security and has contributed critically to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, to reflect recent changes in the strategic environment

[763] To this end, the plan aims to smoothly advance the ongoing restructuring of US F, including the relocation of Yongsan Garrison, the redeployment of the US 2nd Infantry Division, the transfer of 10 major military missions to the ROK military, and the reduction of US F forces

[764] Furthermore, it has established comprehensive plans to develop the ROK-US Alliance into a comprehensive and dynamic alliance in the long term

[765] In particular, the relocation of Yongsan Garrison is scheduled to be completed by 2008, and the relocation of the US 2nd Infantry Division will involve the consolidation of minor bases north of the Han River into the Dongducheon and Uijeongbu areas by

[766] In the second phase, the main force will be relocated to the Pyeongtaek area

[767] Phase 2 Implementation will be determined after consultation between the ROK and US leadership, taking into account the security situation on the Korean Peninsula

[768] Of the ten major military missions assigned to USFK, the ROK military has already assumed responsibility for the Joint Security Area (JSA) security mission and rear area decontamination operations

[769] Seven other missions, including rapid mine placement, air-to-ground fire range management, and day and night search and rescue, are scheduled to be gradually assumed in 2005 and

[770] Meanwhile, the decision on whether to transfer the task of conducting counter-fire warfare will be made in August 2005 after an assessment of the ROK military's capabilities

[771] Furthermore, the reduction of USFK will be carried out in three stages by 2008, by 12,500 troops, based on the results of consultations between the ROK and the US

[772] Furthermore, to ensure the comprehensive and dynamic development of the ROK-US alliance, the Security Policy Initiative (SPI), which will replace the existing Future of the ROK-US Alliance Development Policy Initiative (FOTA), will focus on discussions on the goals and vision of the future ROK-US alliance, the status and role of USFK, and the development of ROK-US command relations

[773] The Ministry of National Defense expects that this plan will foster national pride and foster conditions for the stable and long-term stationing of USFK

[774] Furthermore, it is expected that the ROK-US alliance will develop into a new alliance suited to the evolving security environment during the Roh Moo-hyun administration, while also expanding the ROK military's leading role in South Korea's defense

[775] Future of the ROK-U.S. Alliance Policy Initiative SPI: Security Policy Initiative Chapter 4: Current Status and Challenges of Our National Defense B. Early Expansion of War Deterrence Capabilities "Early Expansion of War Deterrence Capabilities" refers to prioritizing the early acquisition of military capabilities capable of deterring the ever-present North Korean threat in our security landscape

[776] Simultaneously, we gradually secure core military capabilities to prepare for future, unspecified threats, thereby laying the foundation for a truly independent national defense

[777] To achieve this, the focus of military power development is to establish a so-called "sensor-to-shooter" system capable of detecting targets in real time, making immediate decisions (C4I), and striking them, in line with future warfare patterns

[778] Specifically, plans were reviewed and developed to secure independent surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities capable of controlling the entire Korean Peninsula, establish a "real-time command, control, and communications (C4I) system" across all tactical and strategic units, and expand "strategic strike capabilities against deep-seated targets

[779] The plan also concretized essential force acquisition measures

[780] Regarding reserve forces, relevant laws and organizations were revised, and critical homeland defense supplies were quickly secured to strengthen response capabilities against North Korean special operations forces

[781] Furthermore, base forces will be strengthened by improving the performance of older and older shooter, sensor, and operational execution concept post-war equipment and securing replacement forces

[782] It also includes plans to strengthen the research and development and defense industry base, and to bring our advanced weapons development technology, currently ranked among the top 10 in the world, up to the level of advanced countries by

[807] Section 2: Future-Oriented Development of the ROK-US Alliance Formed on the legal basis of the "Republic of Korea-US Mutual Defense Treaty" signed on October 1, 1953, the ROK-US Alliance has served as the foundation of our security for the past half-century, maintaining peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula and playing a pivotal role in national development, including democracy and economic growth

[808] However, with the rapidly changing domestic and international security landscape since the end of the Cold War, the ROK-US Alliance is facing new challenges

[812] Along with these changes in the domestic and international security environment, the need for progressive transformation of the ROK-US alliance, which forms the foundation of security on the Korean Peninsula, and public expectations are growing

Changes in U.S. Security Strategy and the ROK-U.S. Alliance 2004 APEC Korea-U.S. Summit In response to the changing security environment following the end of the Cold War, the United States shifted from a threat-based strategic planning approach based on specific threats to a capability-based strategic planning approach based on the ability to rapidly respond to a variety of threats

[820] In other words, the strategy shifted from a win-win strategy of simultaneously winning two large-scale wars while strengthening the defense capabilities of the U.S. homeland to a strategy of repelling the enemy in one theater and deterring enemy attacks in another

[821] At the same time, it shifted to a concept of rejecting challenges to U.S. military superiority and proactively eliminating uncertain threats

[822] To realize this security strategic concept, the United States is comprehensively revising and supplementing its alliance strategy, military strategic concept, readiness posture, and military structure, which it has maintained since World War II

[823] It is also pursuing military transformation to make its forces more advanced, more mobile, and lighter

[824] It is also pursuing the realignment of U.S. military bases stationed around the world

[825] The shift from the traditional concept of "fixed bases" to "mobile bases" capable of rapid deployment when and where needed signifies a readjustment of the force structure and base system of US forces stationed overseas

[826] US Forces Korea is also undergoing readjustment under this concept

[827] Under the strategic concept of actively utilizing these shifts in US global strategy, the ROK government is stably managing peace, prosperity, and security on the Korean Peninsula and developing the ROK-US alliance in a future-oriented manner in conjunction with progress in inter-Korean relations

Overview of Peacekeeping Operations [PK0] While the likelihood of large-scale war has decreased since the end of the Cold War, local conflicts stemming from conflicts over ethnicity, religion, territory, and resources are on the rise

[1055] Amidst this shift in the international security environment, international peacekeeping operations have expanded their role and function as "guardians" of global peace and order

[1056] International peacekeeping operations, which contribute to maintaining global peace and stability and enhance national prestige, are recognized as a key national priority today, and are establishing themselves as a key area of military activity in the 21st century

[1057] Peacekeeping operations are divided into UN peacekeeping operations directly led by the UN and multinational peacekeeping operations led by regional organizations or specific countries with UN approval

[1058] UN-led peacekeeping operations began in 1948 with the Palestine Tranquility Observation Mission (UNTSO), and over the past 55 years, approximately one million personnel from over 120 countries have participated in 59 UN peacekeeping missions

[1059] As of November 2004, approximately 66,300 military and police personnel from 102 UN member states were participating in UN peacekeeping operations in 16 regions, including Liberia, Georgia, India, and Pakistan

[1060] Since dispatching an engineer battalion to Somalia (UNOSOM-II) in 1993 at the UN's request, ROK military personnel have been deployed to Angola, Western Sahara, and East Timor

[1061] The Sangnoksu Unit, deployed to East Timor in October 1999, has flawlessly carried out its missions, including maintaining public order, border control, and conducting civil affairs operations, despite domestic controversy and opposition regarding infantry units' participation in peacekeeping operations

[1062] As a result, the unit successfully completed its mission, earning the nickname "Malaimu Pin" (King of the Multinational Force) from local residents

[1063] The unit withdrew completely in October

[1153] Basic Plan for Troop Deployment The mission of the deployed units was to be to cover a specific area of responsibility, providing postwar recovery support and relief activities

[1154] This will support the functioning of autonomous administrative bodies and promote friendly relations

[1155] Local security will be handled by the Iraqi military and police, while our military will provide training

[1156] The unit will consist of approximately 3,600 personnel, including the Seohui and Jema units

[1157] This will include approximately 1,200 personnel for division and brigade commands and direct units, 1,600 for reconstruction support, and approximately 800 for security forces

[1158] This elite force will be deployed to ensure flexible mission execution and minimize friendly casualties

[1159] The initial deployment area was considered to be the Kirkuk region, but the decision was made to establish a "peaceful" area of independent responsibility

[1160] Because the deployment did not conform to the government's principle of "performing a reconstruction support mission," the ROK and the US agreed to change the deployment area to the Erbil region, an autonomous Kurdistan region

[1161] Accordingly, the government confirmed the Erbil region as the deployment area (June 18, 2004) through several on-site investigations and cooperative activities and coordinated the necessary details with the Erbil provincial authorities

[1261] The Armistice Agreement, signed on July 27, 1953, has served as a legal and institutional mechanism for preventing armed conflict and managing crises on the Korean Peninsula

[1262] Despite difficult circumstances, peace on the Korean Peninsula has been maintained stably for the past half-century under the armistice system

[1263] Following the historic inter-Korean summit in 2000, as inter-Korean reconciliation and exchanges and cooperation began in earnest, research was conducted on establishing a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula, aiming to transform the Armistice system, a legacy of the Korean War, into a peace regime that firmly guarantees peace

[1264] The Roh Moo-hyun administration has set "Establishing a Peace Regime on the Korean Peninsula" as a national agenda and is actively pursuing the establishment of peace on the Korean Peninsula

[1265] Considering the importance of establishing a peace regime to the security structure of the Korean Peninsula, the government intends to pursue this in a gradual and phased manner, comprehensively considering the peaceful resolution of the North Korean nuclear issue, changes in North Korea, progress in inter-Korean relations, and the situation in Northeast Asia

[1266] Establishing a Peace Regime on the Korean Peninsula Since the signing of the Armistice Agreement on July 27, 1953, the Armistice Agreement has functioned as a legal and institutional mechanism for preventing armed conflict and managing crises on the Korean Peninsula

[1267] In particular, the Military Armistice Commission (MAC) and the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission (NNSC) have actively worked to effectively ensure the implementation of the Armistice Agreement even under difficult circumstances, resulting in stable peace on the Korean Peninsula for the past half-century

[1268] However, after a South Korean general was appointed as the senior representative to the UNC Military Armistice Commission on March 25, 1991, the North unilaterally refused to participate in the plenary session of the Military Armistice Commission, preventing the Commission from operating normally

[1269] The Military Armistice Commission Secretary-General's Meeting and the Chiefs of Staff Meeting took over its functions

[1270] Despite agreeing to abide by the current Armistice Agreement until a solid state of peace was established on the Korean Peninsula in the "Inter-Korean Basic Agreement," which came into effect in 1992, the North began a series of measures aimed at nullifying the armistice system in

[1271] Following the withdrawal of the Czech delegation on April 3, 1993, and the withdrawal of the North Korean Military Armistice Commission on April 28, 1994, the so-called "Korean People's Army Panmunjom Delegation" was established on May 24 of the same year, the Chinese military representative to the Military Armistice Commission was withdrawn on December 15, and the Polish delegation was forcibly withdrawn on February

[1272] Meanwhile, the South Korean government and the United Nations Command maintained the position that the Military Armistice Commission and the Neutral Supervisory Commission should continue to operate as long as the Armistice Agreement remains in place, and the UNC Military Armistice Commission and the Neutral Supervisory Commission operated normally

[1273] However, on March 2, 1995, the North made its intention to nullify the Armistice Agreement even more explicit by officially proposing to hold general-level talks between the United States and North Korea in place of the Military Armistice Commission

[1274] The Ministry of National Defense and the United Nations Command (UNC) concluded that a responsible dialogue channel was needed within the framework of the armistice system to manage the crisis on the Korean Peninsula

[1275] Therefore, on February 11, 1998, they proposed to the North Korean side a general-level meeting between the UNC and the North Korean military

[1276] Following the North's positive response, seven rounds of secretary-general and staff officer contacts were held between March 3 and May

[1277] An agreement on the procedures for general-level talks between the UNC and the North Korean military was signed on June

[1278] Following the first general-level meeting between the UNC and the North Korean military on June 23, 1998, a total of 14 meetings were held through September

[1279] These meetings primarily focused on identifying the causes and responsibilities for violations of the Armistice Agreement and exchanging opinions on matters of mutual military concern

[1280] In particular, the 12th and 14th talks signed and implemented an agreement on the opening of some areas of the Demilitarized Zone in connection with the construction of inter-Korean railways and roads, thereby creating an environment for active inter-Korean exchange and cooperation projects utilizing the East and West Sea railways and roads

[1281] However, due to differences in opinions between the UN Command and the North Korean military regarding the agenda for general-level talks, no additional talks have been held since the 14th meeting

[1282] The UN Command insists on regularizing general-level talks between the UN Command and the North Korean military to discuss compliance with the Armistice Agreement and easing military tensions

[1283] On the other hand, the North has refused to participate in the talks, demanding that the UN Command and the North Korean military prioritize the formation of a trilateral military organization involving South Korea, North Korea, and the United States to replace the general-level talks

[1284] Easing Tensions on the Korean Peninsula and Establishing a Peace Regime Since March 2003, the North has refused regular contact with the Military Armistice Commission staff officers and has demanded the dissolution of the United Nations Command at every opportunity

[1285] The government maintains its position of steadfast adherence to the current Armistice Agreement until a solid peace state is established on the Korean Peninsula

[1286] The government is striving to normalize the functions of the Military Armistice Commission, the general-level talks between the UN and North Korean militaries held within its framework, and the Neutral Supervision and Inspection Commission

[1287] Furthermore, the government is closely coordinating with the UN Command to ensure active inter-Korean exchange and cooperation within the armistice framework, and is holding talks between the military authorities of the two Koreas to discuss military support measures

[1288] B. Establishing a Peace Regime Establishing a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula means transforming the armistice system, a legacy of the Korean War, into a peace regime that firmly guarantees peace

[1289] The goal of establishing a peace regime is to eliminate the deep-rooted mutual distrust and confrontation-driven hostility between the two Koreas, achieve permanent peace on the Korean Peninsula, and, based on this, lay the foundation for national coexistence and co-prosperity

[1290] Easing Tensions on the Korean Peninsula and Establishing a Peace Regime The participatory government has set "establishing a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula" as a national agenda and is actively pursuing the establishment of peace on the Korean Peninsula

[1291] As establishing a peace regime involves changing the armistice system that has governed the Korean Peninsula for the past half-century, the government intends to pursue this goal gradually and step by step, comprehensively considering factors such as the peaceful resolution of the North Korean nuclear issue, changes in North Korea, progress in inter-Korean relations, and the situation in Northeast Asia

[1292] To establish a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula, the government is continuously strengthening inter-Korean dialogue and cooperation to lay the foundation for the institutionalization of peace

[1293] Furthermore, through diplomatic efforts, the government is fostering an atmosphere of international understanding and cooperation for the establishment of a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula

[1294] The government firmly upholds the principle of North and South Korea as parties involved in the process of establishing a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula

[1295] The government aims to achieve the conclusion of a peace agreement and the establishment of a peace regime in a way that both North and South Korea are parties and the international community supports, guarantees, and actively participates in this process

[1296] The peace regime established on the Korean Peninsula through this process is expected to serve as a major driving force for enhanced security and economic cooperation in Northeast Asia and significantly contribute to world peace

[1297] The North Korean nuclear issue arose in late 1989, following the discovery of North Korea's Yongbyon nuclear facility by a French commercial satellite

[1298] During the process of conducting nuclear inspections by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), North Korea's past nuclear activities (plutonium extraction) were confirmed

[1299] After numerous twists and turns, the North Korean nuclear issue appeared to be resolved on October 21, 1994, when the US-North Korea Agreed Framework (Agreed Framework) was signed in Geneva

[1300] The agreement stipulated that North Korea would freeze its nuclear facilities in exchange for the US providing 500,000 tons of heavy oil annually and two 1,000 MWe light-water reactors

[1301] However, in early October 2002, North Korea admitted to its enriched uranium (HEU) program, leading to the resumption of the three principles for resolving the North Korean nuclear issue: Non-acceptance of North Korea's nuclear program Peaceful resolution through dialogue An active role for the Republic of Korea AF: Agreed Framework HEU: Highly Enriched Uranium The North Korean nuclear issue has resurfaced

[1302] North Korea's Nuclear Freeze Lifting Measures: December 12, 2002 Declaration of Lifting of Nuclear Freeze December 21-24, 2002 Removal of Seals on Nuclear Freeze Facility December 31, 2002 Expulsion of IAEA Inspectors January 10, 2003 Declaration of Withdrawal from the NPT February 26, 2003 5MWe Reactor Restarted April 18, 2003 Reprocessing of Spent Fuel Rods Insisting on Progress The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization (KEDO) regarded North Korea's uranium enrichment program as a clear violation of the Agreed Framework and suspended heavy fuel oil supplies to North Korea in December

[1303] In response, North Korea demanded the US withdraw its hostile policy toward North Korea and the conclusion of a non-aggression treaty, and pushed ahead with a series of nuclear freeze lifting measures, escalating the nuclear crisis

[1304] The government maintains that North Korea's nuclear development poses a grave threat to the stability and peace of the Korean Peninsula and Northeast Asia

[1305] Under no circumstances should North Korea possess nuclear weapons, and the government's position is to fundamentally and comprehensively resolve the North Korean nuclear issue through peaceful means

[1306] This means that the issue must be resolved by ensuring that North Korea dismantles all nuclear programs, undergoes verification through international inspections, and prevents concerns about nuclear weapons from resurfacing

[1307] To this end, the government is actively pursuing the Six-Party Talks through policy coordination among South Korea, the United States, and Japan, and close consultations with China and Russia

[1308] It is also actively persuading North Korea to give up its nuclear weapons through various inter-Korean dialogue channels

[1309] In particular, the government emphasizes that worsening the situation or possessing nuclear weapons will in no way contribute to the survival of the regime, and has made clear its position that it will provide large-scale aid to North Korea if it gives up its nuclear weapons

[1310] Thanks to active dialogue efforts by the relevant countries, the first round of the Six-Party Talks (August 27-29, 2003) was held in Beijing, China

[1311] Following this, two more rounds of the Six-Party Talks (April 25-28, 2003; June 23-26, 2003) and working-level meetings (May 12-14, 2003; June 21-22, 2003) were held

[1312] At the third round of the Six-Party Talks held in June 2004, South Korea, North Korea, and the United States presented concrete solutions to the problem, laying the foundation for the North Korean nuclear issue to enter the full-scale negotiation phase

[1313] However, since the third round of the Six-Party Talks, North Korea has maintained its existing theoretical position and has delayed the holding of the fourth round of the Six-Party Talks

[1314] Given the significant differences in views among the relevant countries regarding specific methods for resolving the North Korean nuclear issue, it is expected that further dialogue and compromise will be necessary before a concrete agreement can be reached

[1315] Going forward, the government will continue to make multifaceted efforts to peacefully resolve the North Korean nuclear issue, including developing concrete alternatives to key issues and encouraging North Korea to make strategic decisions through various channels

[1335] Inter-Korean General-Level Military Talks At the 13th Inter-Korean Ministerial Talks (February 6, 2004), both sides agreed that full-scale consultations on easing military tensions and building trust on the Korean Peninsula were necessary for the stable development of inter-Korean relations

[1337] Accordingly, South Korea proposed holding talks with North Korea (February 12, 2004), but North Korea remained unresponsive

[1338] However, at the 14th Inter-Korean Ministerial Talks (May 7, 2004), both sides re-agreed to hold general-level military talks

[1339] North Korea proposed holding the first round of talks in the Kumgangsan area on May

[1340] Substantive discussions on holding the talks began

[1341] However, during these practical discussions, the two sides experienced difficulties due to the issue of senior delegate rank

[1342] Finally, on May 25, they exchanged a list of delegations, led by a first-star general, and the first round of general-level military talks was held at Kumgangsan on May

[1343] First Inter-Korean General-Level Talks At these talks, the South Korean side proposed specific measures to prevent accidental clashes in the West Sea, including: ① the installation and operation of a direct telephone line between the West Sea Fleet Commanders, ② the establishment and operation of a shared frequency between patrol vessels, ③ the establishment and use of visual signals (light and air currents) between patrol vessels, and ④ the exchange of information related to crackdowns on illegal fishing activities by third-country fishing vessels

[1344] The North argued that the urgent task was to cease provocative propaganda activities and eliminate the means of such activities in the Military Demarcation Line area, and that discussions should begin on this issue first

[1345] At the second Inter-Korean General-Level Talks held at Seoraksan Mountain from June 3rd to 4th, the two sides adopted and entered into force the "Agreement on the Prevention of Accidental Clashes in the West Sea, the Cessation of Propaganda Activities in the Military Demarcation Line Area, and the Removal of Athletes

[1346] This agreement, which linked the "West Sea issue" and the "Propaganda issue," was reached in a package to establish mutual military contact between the two Koreas, which has not made any progress on substantive issues related to easing military tensions, prevent accidental clashes in the West Sea, where two military clashes occurred, thereby easing military tensions on the Korean Peninsula, and protect the livelihoods of our fishermen by preventing illegal fishing by third-country fishing vessels

[1347] The first inter-Korean general-level military talks were held in Kaesong from June 10th to 12th to discuss specific implementation measures for the above agreement

[1348] At these talks, the two sides adopted and entered into force the "Agreement on the Cessation of Propaganda Activities and Removal of Propaganda Means" (Section 4: Easing Tensions on the Korean Peninsula and Establishing a Peace Regime Defense White Paper 133 Chapter 4: Current Status and Tasks of Our National Defense

[1349] Following this agreement, the two sides conducted operational tests of the international merchant marine common network and various communication methods, including air currents and flashing lights, between inter-Korean vessels in the West Sea on June 14th, and ceased all propaganda activities in the Military Demarcation Line area from June 15th

[1350] On June 16, the dismantling of the propaganda unit facilities and equipment began

[1351] The second working-level representative meeting of the inter-Korean general-level military talks held on June 29th and 30th confirmed the results of the first phase of the mine removal from the Military Demarcation Line area and discussed regularizing test communications between North and South Korean vessels in the West Sea

[1352] However, due to differences in opinion regarding the athlete removal, the two sides held a meeting of senior representatives on July 5th

[1353] They agreed to commence the second phase of athlete removal on July 6th and faithfully implement the agreements regarding the West Sea issue

[1354] Communications between North and South Korean vessels in the West Sea However, with the complete suspension of dialogue between the North and South Korean authorities in mid-July, the inter-Korean general-level military talks and working-level representative meetings were suspended

[1355] The dismantling of the propaganda unit in the Military Demarcation Line area, which was approximately 50-60% progress, has not been implemented since August 13th

[1356] Meanwhile, communications between South and North Korean vessels in the West Sea via the international merchant marine common network and information exchange on illegal fishing vessels are continuing

[1357] Going forward, the military plans to hold inter-Korean general-level military talks or working-level representative talks as soon as possible to discuss with North Korea ways to implement previously agreed-upon matters, including the currently suspended removal of propaganda equipment

[1358] Military Support for Inter-Korean Exchange and Cooperation Projects Under the "Peace and Prosperity Policy," the participatory government is expanding inter-Korean economic cooperation projects, including the connection of inter-Korean railways and roads, the development of the Kaesong Industrial Complex, and Mount Kumgang tourism

[1359] In response to these government policies, the Ministry of National Defense is actively supporting inter-Korean exchange and cooperation projects in the military sector

Status of Unrepatriated ROK POWs In accordance with the Armistice Agreement signed on July 27, 1953, the UN forces and the Communist forces exchanged prisoners of war

[1383] However, a significant number of ROK POWs held in North Korea were not repatriated against their will

[1384] The UNC continued to request the repatriation of these ROK POWs through the Military Armistice Commission until the early 1960s

[1385] However, as North Korea maintained its position that "there were not a single ROK POW," the issue remained unresolved, with no proper solution found

[1386] Amidst this situation, the return of Second Lieutenant Cho Chang-ho, a South Korean POW, in October 1994 brought the issue of South Korean POWs to national attention

[1387] To determine the status of unrepatriated South Korean POWs, the Ministry of National Defense, through a review of missing persons reports and military registers, released a list of 19,409 missing persons from the Korean War in October

[1388] This list is believed to include a significant number of unrepatriated South Korean POWs

[1389] Based on the testimonies of defectors and 47 repatriated South Korean POWs, it is estimated that 538 South Korean POWs were still alive in North Korea as of December

[1390] B. Government Efforts to Resolve the Issue The government maintains its position that it will actively pursue the repatriation of South Korean POWs through all channels, as part of its "national duty and obligation

[1391] The government has consistently raised the issue of repatriation of South Korean POWs through international organizations and urged a fundamental resolution of the issue during negotiations with North Korea

[1392] However, due to North Korea's refusal to discuss the issue, direct repatriation efforts have yet to yield tangible results

[1393] As a practical solution, the government is actively promoting exchanges of letters and reunions, broadly categorizing the issue of separated families

[1394] With the completion of the separated family reunion center in the Geumgangsan region and the significant improvement in inter-Korean relations, it is expected that more POW reunions will take place

[1395] In response to the recent significant increase in the number of South Korean POWs residing in third countries, the government has implemented a series of institutional reforms to facilitate their prompt repatriation and stable settlement

[1396] Regulations on the Repatriation of POWs (Prime Minister's Instruction No. 448) was enacted and promulgated (January 19, 2004) to clearly define the division of duties and procedures for the relevant ministries regarding the repatriation of POWs residing in third countries

[1397] These regulations were also applied to the repatriation of spouses and direct descendants of POWs

[1398] Furthermore, the "Regulations on the Handling of POW Affairs, etc." (Ministry of National Defense Instruction No. 746) was enacted and promulgated (March 22, 2004) to clearly define the division of duties and procedures for each department and agency related to POW affairs

[1399] These government efforts have led to a significant increase in the repatriation of ROK POWs and their families residing in third countries since

[1400] Pursuant to the Act on the Treatment of Prisoners of War, promulgated on January 29, 1999, the government provides these returning POWs with pensions, settlement allowances, and housing support, thereby supporting their stable domestic settlement

[1401] Furthermore, the Ministry of National Defense annually invites returning POWs, accompanied by their spouses, to security site tours and meetings

[1402] Discharge Ceremony for Returning POWs, 1st Lieutenant Cho Chang-ho. The government will continue to pursue the repatriation of ROK POWs residing in third countries and their families, while also raising the issue of POW repatriation with North Korea through various channels

[1403] Furthermore, the government will explore various measures to ensure the stable domestic settlement of these returning POWs and their families

[1404] Section 5: Building Self-Defense Capabilities Our military has inevitably relied on the ROK-US combined defense system for a significant portion of its war deterrence, and this has left us with inadequate independent war-fighting capabilities

[1405] Recently, amidst the progress in inter-Korean reconciliation and cooperation, our strategic environment is rapidly changing

[1406] This includes the dual security situation, with the ever-present military threat from North Korea, and the ongoing readjustment of US Forces Korea (USFK) following the US's review of its global defense posture

[1407] Consequently, the need to build a military capable of proactively responding to this evolving strategic environment and effectively deterring the current North Korean threat is more urgent than ever

[1408] Direction of Military Capacity Building With the groundbreaking advancements in science and technology, the traditional form of warfare, which pursued territorial security and mass destruction, is shifting to a new form of warfare, one that paralyzes the enemy's intelligence capabilities and strikes at their core

[1409] To wage such a war, superior surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities, automated command, control, and communications systems, long-range strike capabilities against deep targets, and mobility will be essential

[1410] Considering the ever-present North Korean threat, our security situation requires us to prioritize rapidly expanding our military capabilities to deter this threat, while simultaneously gradually securing core forces to prepare for future, unspecified threats

[1411] To achieve this, our military development strategy will involve establishing a "sensor-to-shooter" system suited to the nature of future warfare

[1412] Furthermore, we will secure independent surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities capable of controlling the entire Korean Peninsula, establish a real-time command, control, and communications (C4I) system spanning tactical, operational, and strategic echelons, and expand our "strategic strike capabilities against deep targets

[1413] Section 5: Building Self-Defense Capabilities Chapter 4: Current Status and Challenges of Our National Defense Defense Force Investment Projects and Research and Development A. Goals and Directions of Force Investment Projects The Ministry of National Defense has set a goal of deploying weapons, equipment, and supplies with the performance required by the military at an economical cost and in a timely manner

[1414] To achieve this, it has proposed five major directions

[1415] First, to secure the technologies necessary for the development of future cutting-edge weapons, the Agency for Defense Development will be developed into a technology development focused research institute and new specialized research centers will be established

[1416] This will innovate the research and development system and expand R&D investment

[1417] Second, to ensure economic acquisition of weapons systems, performance improvements to existing weapons and equipment will be promoted and the principle of competition will be expanded throughout the acquisition process

[1418] Third, when developing weapons systems domestically or purchasing them from overseas, force integration support elements will be secured in a packaged manner and interoperability and operability with existing weapons systems will be ensured to ensure integrated force performance

[1419] Fourth, defense investment projects with significant ripple effects on domestic industrial development will be promoted as national projects and utilize the national industrial base to the fullest extent

[1420] Fifth, the entire acquisition process will be transparently disclosed, irrational elements in systems and procedures will be identified and improved, specialized personnel will be trained, and personnel management systems will be developed to enhance transparency, rationality, and professionalism in acquisition work

[1421] Goals Timely and economically deploy weapons, equipment, and supplies with the performance required by the military Directions Secure core technologies necessary for the development of future advanced weapons Promote economical weapon system acquisition projects Ensure integrated force development Strengthen connectivity with national industrial development Enhance rationality, professionalism, and transparency in acquisition work Section 5 Building Self-Defense Capabilities B. Improvement of the Defense Acquisition System The Ministry of National Defense is continuously analyzing and improving all areas of the acquisition system to ensure its transparent and efficient operation

[1422] In particular, to strengthen the institutional framework of the acquisition management system, relevant laws, procedures, and organizations are being reorganized

[1423] Improving transparency and fairness in decision-making regarding military investment projects Establishing mid-term defense plans, budget allocation, approving research and development plans, selecting aircraft types, and approving the execution of major projects are sensitive to the interests of each military branch, agency, and defense industry, making it crucial to ensure transparency, fairness, and accountability in decision-making

[1424] Therefore, the approval process has been improved to prevent arbitrary decision-making due to the concentration of authority and responsibility in the hands of decision-makers

[1425] Military investment projects have been deliberated and decided by a conference since May

[1426] When necessary, the system has been transitioned to an open decision-making process, allowing for the participation of officials from relevant government ministries and civilian experts

[1427] Improving economic feasibility through improved overseas procurement systems and procedures Inconsistent decision-making when purchasing weapons from overseas not only leads to significant waste and loss of defense budgets, but also has the potential to escalate into diplomatic issues if fairness is questioned

[1428] Therefore, to fundamentally improve these issues, we have institutionalized the establishment of a "Project Promotion Strategy" to maintain consistency in project implementation

[1429] Furthermore, we have improved the system to ensure fair and economical procurement by requiring aircraft types to be determined through competitive bidding

[1430] We actively reflect the opinions of military and agencies that raise requirements from the early stages of R&D. Core technology R&D requirements are comprehensively reviewed and submitted to the Ministry of National Defense by the Joint Chiefs of Staff

[1431] Furthermore, prototype suppliers are involved in the basic design of prototypes alongside the prototype manufacturer, enabling efficient prototype production

[1432] Furthermore, we are promoting the establishment and operation of specialized defense-related research centers in academia to establish core foundational technologies, cultivate defense research personnel and expand their base, and carry out core technology development

[1433] Aircraft Type Determination Method Foreign companies that meet the military's requirements are granted bid qualifications through testing, evaluation, and negotiation

[1434] • Decision is made through competitive bidding among companies

[1435] Establishing a Preparatory System for Major Acquisition Projects. For major projects, pre-analysis activities were strengthened before commencement to enable early identification and resolution of potential issues during project implementation

[1436] To efficiently perform cost estimation, pre-negotiation and cost analysis procedures were improved to establish an organic cooperative system

[1437] Establishment of the Procurement Headquarters as a Dedicated Contracting Agency Contracting work for major military projects was transferred to the Procurement Headquarters, allowing the Procurement Headquarters to take full responsibility for contracting

[1451] Section 5 Building Self-Defense Defense Capabilities Research and Development and the Defense Industry Development of Defense Research and Development Policy Future warfare is expected to shift from equipment- and manpower-centered mobile warfare to knowledge-based information warfare due to advancements in high-speed communication and computer technology

[1452] Accordingly, advanced countries are aggressively investing in R&D to acquire surveillance satellites equipped with ultra-precision imagery sensors, underwater surveillance systems utilizing high-sensitivity complex underwater acoustic and non-acoustic sensors, and various intelligent guided weapons

[1453] They are also strengthening core technology protection policies to maintain a firm technological edge

[1454] However, unlike the global trend, our military acquisition paradigm is heavily focused on weapons systems and the import of foreign products

[1455] This has led to insufficient investment in domestic technology development and advanced countries' avoidance of technology transfer, widening the technological gap with advanced countries and perpetuating a vicious cycle of dependence on advanced countries for advanced equipment and core technologies

[1456] Figure 4-10] Korea's R&D Level (as of 2004) 144 2004 Defense White Paper Domestic Level Jun 70 allalu ※Mobility, firepower, guided weapons, intelligence

[1457] In the field of electronic warfare, we maintain a level higher than the average of advanced countries

[1458] To break this vicious cycle, the Ministry of National Defense published the "Defense Research and Development Policy" in 2004, which outlines the goals, development directions, and R&D projects for defense research and development (R&D) in weapon systems and core technologies

[1459] This laid the foundation for systematic and goal-oriented R&D. Building on this foundation, we will pursue a robust R&D policy

[1460] By 2010, we will acquire the core technologies necessary for advanced weapon R&D, thereby achieving technological advancement

[1461] By 2020, we will secure the ability to independently develop future advanced weapon systems

[1462] This will be a comprehensive effort to build self-defense capabilities

[1463] Section 5: Building Self-Defense Capabilities The ROK military's defense R&D policy aims to develop core force systems and technological innovation to simultaneously meet the needs of building a future science and technology force and the national science and technology development policy

[1464] The following priorities are being selected and implemented

[1465] First, to advance the defense R&D system, in 2003, high-value-added defense science and technology development projects were reflected in the "Participatory Government's 2003-07 National Science and Technology Basic Plan" to promote defense R&D in conjunction with government-wide science and technology policies

[1466] At the Ministry of National Defense level, the "Defense Research and Development Policy" explicitly stipulates that industry and specialized research institutes should lead development in core defense technologies where the private sector holds a dominant position, thereby boldly expanding the outsourcing of core technology development

[1467] Furthermore, the Civilian-Military Dual-Use Technology Development Project, jointly promoted by four ministries since 1999, has been continuously promoted to simultaneously enhance security capabilities and industrial competitiveness

[1468] Furthermore, five new specialized research centers focusing on specific military technology fields have been established to integrate the academic community's outstanding technological potential into core technology development and encourage the participation of talented individuals in defense technology development

[1469] Furthermore, the "Defense Science and Technology Basic Research Plan" was developed to establish a systematic research plan for basic defense fields, allowing academia to conduct focused research

[1470] Second, we are striving to foster the Agency for Defense Development (ADD) as a cutting-edge research institute, contributing to the scientific advancement of the military, conducting domestic research and development of cutting-edge core weapon systems, and playing a central role in eliminating dependence on foreign sources for related core technologies

[1471] To this end, we are pursuing a plan to have the Agency for Defense Development join the "Scientists and Engineers Mutual Aid Association," a pension system for researchers at government-funded research institutes, to secure a talented workforce in the defense science field

[1472] We will also continue to improve the research conditions and welfare of researchers, including raising wages

[1473] Third, a prerequisite for revitalizing defense R&D is a dramatic increase in the absolute level of defense R&D spending

[1474] While major advanced countries have maintained R&D spending at over 10% of their defense budgets for the past five years, South Korea's investment remains at half that level

[1475] The Ministry of National Defense will improve the conditions for defense R&D by gradually increasing defense R&D spending to 7% of the national defense budget in 2008 and 10% in 2015, in accordance with the cooperative self-reliant defense promotion plan

[1476] Specialized Research Centers To integrate the outstanding technological potential of academia into core technology development and encourage the participation of talented individuals in defense technology development, they were commissioned to conduct research focused on specific technological fields

[1477] By 2003, a total of KRW 35.2 billion was provided in support of 70 projects, with 318 professors and 1,315 students from 125 institutions participating in this research

[1503] Establishing a Domestic Defense Industry Foundation The "Special Measures Act on Military Procurement," enacted in 1973 to foster the defense industry, has been supplemented and developed into the "Special Measures Act on the Defense Industry

[1504] This includes specialization and affiliation systems, a designation system for defense products and companies, a defense industry promotion fund system, and special contracting, cost, and tax incentives

[1505] As a result, our defense industry has achieved remarkable growth, even producing advanced precision weapons

[1506] As of the end of 2003, 82 companies were producing and supplying 1,235 defense products

[1507] However, despite its apparent growth, our defense industry is facing significant management challenges, with an average operating rate of only 50% due to difficulties in generating further domestic demand

[1509] We are implementing a multifaceted development and support policy

[1510] First, we are enhancing the competitiveness of the defense industry by adjusting the specialization and integration system

[1511] Introduced in 1983 to prevent duplication of investment and promote technological development in the defense industry, the specialization and integration system, initially operated as a monopoly, was transformed into a competitive system in 1999 to encourage the participation of companies with superior technological capabilities and strengthen the competitiveness of the defense industry

[1512] As of 2003, 29 companies and 31 items were designated for specialization, and 48 companies and 86 items were designated for integration

[1513] The Ministry of National Defense plans to continuously reorganize the existing specialization and integration systems, taking into account domestic industrial technology development trends

[1514] In the long term, we plan to scale back the system to focus on core strategic and non-wing weapon systems

[1515] Second, we will strengthen the foundation of the defense industry by efficiently operating the defense product and company designation system

[1516] The defense articles and company designation system, introduced and implemented to ensure the stable procurement and quality assurance of militaryspecific equipment and supplies difficult to procure under market economic principles, reflects the development trends of the domestic civilian industry since the 1990s

[1517] Furthermore, to secure competitiveness through increased competition among companies, the designation of defense articles is restricted, with a focus on weapon systems, as much as possible

[1518] For already designated defense articles, designation cancellation is reviewed every two years

[1553] Major Improvements to the Defense Acquisition System Maintaining the rationality and consistency of requirements planning Enhancing the efficiency of overseas procurement work Improving the domestic R&D management system Establishing an efficient financial resource management system Improving the rationality of military supplies procurement work Strengthening the competitiveness of defense industry companies Ensuring transparency in military facility construction work Organizational redesign and improved personnel management Improving the evaluation system Continuous monitoring system Among the 10 major improvement tasks, regarding organizational redesign and improved personnel management, it was agreed to establish the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (tentative name), an independent organization that will oversee acquisition policy and execution functions and strengthen expertise, transparency, and accountability

Defense Information and Policy Directions Goals of Defense Informatization Defense informatization utilizes information technology (IT) and management innovation techniques to transform the entire defense work system into an information and knowledge-centered environment

[1559] The goal of defense informatization is to foster an intelligent, ubiquitous-based information military by establishing an integrated information system that enables the sharing of information and knowledge during both wartime and peacetime, and the real-time distribution and utilization of such information

[1560] Defense information aims to build an integrated defense information system that guarantees interoperability between the battlefield management information system and the resource management information system, based on the defense informatization environment and information and communication infrastructure

[1561] This ensures real-time information distribution and utilization between the battlefield management information system and the resource management information system

[1562] Defense Integrated Information System Battlefield Management •Resource Management Interoperability Information System Information System Information System Information and Communication Infrastructure Policy and Implementation Strategy

[1563] The defense informatization policy aims to economically and efficiently build a user-centered information system (combatant) based on interoperability and standardization through cooperation between the public, private, and military sectors, using a goal-oriented, incremental, and evolutionary approach

[1564] The implementation strategy is divided into three stages, as illustrated in Figure

[1565] Phase-by-Phase Implementation Strategy Phase 1 ('05-'09) Establishment of an Information and Communication Network-centered Infrastructure Establishment Phase 2 ('10-'15) Integrated Information System Completion Establishment of a Ubiquitous Infrastructure Improvement of Application System Performance and System Integration Establishment of a Ubiquitous Environment Phase 3 ('16-'20) Establishment of Next-Generation Advanced Systems Establishment of an Intelligent Advanced Information System Section

[1566] B. Improving the Defense Informatization Environment The defense informatization environment consists of systems and procedures, organizations and personnel, interoperability and standardization, and maintenance of a civil-government-military cooperative system

[1567] It is continuously being promoted by reflecting trends in information technology development

[1568] First, regarding systems and procedures, we are establishing and revising relevant guidelines for the defense planning and acquisition management documentation system, developing information technology project evaluation and supervision procedures, and introducing and developing efficient, state-of-the-art project management techniques and systems

[1569] Second, regarding organizational and personnel management, we are revitalizing the Chief Information Officer (CIO) system and efficiently strengthening the organization and personnel for policy formulation and implementation and technology research

[1570] Third, regarding interoperability and standardization, we are establishing a common operating environment and data sharing environment to ensure the military-wide sharing and joint use of defense information systems and information resources

[1571] We are promoting system integration with weapons systems, such as surveillance and strike systems, centered on the C4I system, and establishing a certification system to ensure interoperability

[1572] Fourth, to maintain a civil-government-military cooperative system, we are promoting the launch of a consultative body to maximize the use of the national informatization foundation and hosting events such as the Defense Information Technology Symposium to facilitate technological exchanges with military informatization operations

[1676] Promoting Welfare to Improve the Quality of Life Soldiers perform their duties in special environments

[1677] The military's missions are always fraught with inherent risks, and most military bases are located in remote or isolated areas

[1678] Professional soldiers, including non-commissioned officers and above, face difficulties in securing their children's education and housing due to frequent relocations

[1679] Compared to general civil servants, their young age and limited opportunities for re-employment after discharge result in lower job security

[1680] The housing facilities for soldiers living on base are often outdated, and leisure facilities are severely lacking compared to the number of personnel on duty

[1681] These issues lower soldier morale and create structural problems that hinder the defense sector's ability to attract talented personnel, hindering the achievement of its goal of securing national security

[1682] Therefore, the Ministry of National Defense has established and is implementing various welfare measures to enhance the "quality of life" of soldiers, encouraging their motivation for military service and boosting morale

[1683] These measures include improving the military salary and allowance system, securing military officers' quarters comparable to public housing, installing bunktype barracks and leisure facilities for barrack life, improving soldier food and clothing quality, and improving the medical environment

[1684] We are dramatically improving the working conditions of military personnel by improving the military welfare system and providing educational support for military children

[1685] Furthermore, we are strengthening employment support measures for discharged soldiers and improving the military pension system to enhance job stability

[1686] Improving the Military Salary and Allowance System Despite the existence of the Military Personnel Compensation Act, the current military compensation is subject to the compensation and allowance regulations for general civil servants, failing to properly reflect the unique characteristics of military service

[1687] Therefore, considering the challenging military service conditions, such as early retirement, difficulties in finding new employment, and restrictions on children's education, the current Military Personnel Compensation Act should be revised to reflect the current reality and adopt an independent compensation system

[1688] Promoting Welfare for an Improved Quality of Life

[1691] To reflect an appropriate rate of increase, related laws and regulations, including the enactment of the "Military Personnel Compensation Act Enforcement Decree" based on the "Military Personnel Compensation Act," will be revised

Characteristics of the Military Pension System The military pension system aims to contribute to the stability and welfare of soldiers and their bereaved families by providing appropriate benefits upon retirement after faithful service, retirement due to physical or mental disability, death, or recuperation from occupational illness or injury

[1799] This military pension system was incorporated into the Civil Servants Pension Act, enacted on January 1, 1960, and was separated from the Civil Servants Pension on January 2, 1963, in consideration of the specific characteristics of military service

[1800] Soldiers must perform their duties, even at the risk of their lives, to protect the lives and property of their nation and its citizens

[1801] Their private lives are restricted by emergency standby, operations, training, and frequent relocations

[1802] If they fail to advance during the career stability period of around 45-56, they are discharged early, regardless of their will

[1803] After discharge, employment opportunities are limited because the knowledge acquired during service is no longer relevant to society

[1804] Furthermore, the military pension system includes periods prior to 1959, before the enactment of the Military Pension Act, in the period without requiring contributions

[1805] Furthermore, combat service in the Korean War and Vietnam War is tripled

[1806] Due to the nature of the military organization, early discharges result in longer pension periods compared to other pension recipients

[1807] Consequently, the system has struggled to secure adequate funds from the outset

[1808] Public hearing on the revision of the Military Pension Act: A lifetime of national security, a lifetime of national responsibility

[1812] B. Efforts to Improve the Military Pension System Consequently, to address the military pension deficit and stabilize pension finances, the government revised the Military Pension Act in

[1813] The individual and state contribution rates were increased from 7.5% to 8.5%, and the pension increase method was changed from the rate of increase in incumbent compensation to the consumer price index, and the pension calculation standard was changed from the final monthly salary to the three-year average monthly salary

[1814] Furthermore, institutional mechanisms were established to stabilize pension finances, including legislation to provide national treasury support in cases where the budget for pension payments is insufficient and to establish a liability reserve fund to stabilize pension finances

[1815] Trends in Individual and National Contribution Rate Increases Accordingly, in 2005, in consultation with relevant government ministries, detailed standards for the accumulation of liability reserve funds will be established, laying the foundation for accumulating adequate funds

[1816] Furthermore, the currently dual pension system, consisting of the Military Pension Special Account and the Military Pension Fund, will be unified into a single fund

[1817] In the mid- to long-term, the Military Pension Service will be established and operated to actively increase the fund, thereby stabilizing pension finances

[1870] The Need for Securing Appropriate Defense Budgets Our military must pursue "cooperative self-reliant defense" to secure deterrence capabilities against North Korea, while also fostering morale and welfare for soldiers and fostering the development of defense informatization and science to maximize combat effectiveness

[1871] However, compared to the expansion of the national economy and government finances since the 1980s, the allocation of resources to the defense sector has continued to trend downward, resulting in significant difficulties not only in building military capabilities but also in maintaining existing forces

[1872] A. Defense Expenditure Allocation Trends and Current Status of Defense Operations While the nominal amount of defense spending has steadily increased, defense operations have been under pressure to tighten due to natural increases in costs, including rising general prices, the increasing cost of advanced weapon systems due to scientific and technological advancements, realistic wage levels resulting from rising national income, and increasing military welfare needs

[1873] Defense expenditures as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) remained at around 6% until the early 1980s, but fell to 2.7% in

[1874] The share of defense spending in the government budget has also been steadily decreasing, from 34.7% in the early 1980s to 15.8% in

[1876] Furthermore, insufficient research and development (R&D) funding is delaying the development of independent R&D capabilities and the domestic production of key weapon systems

[1877] The lack of defense funding is also negatively impacting the operation of existing forces

[1878] The supply rate of training ammunition is only around 90%, and the availability of fuel for flight training is limited, resulting in fighter pilots' annual flight training hours falling short of the appropriate level

[1880] In this situation, self-help measures have been taken to improve the efficiency of national defense operations, such as budget reductions and zero-based budget reviews

[1881] However, these measures have been limited in overcoming the overall deteriorating operating conditions

[1882] Chapter 4: Current Status and Challenges of Our National Defense B. Defense Expenditures in Response to National Capabilities Defense spending supports economic growth by deterring war and maintaining peace

[1883] Economic growth, in turn, leads to investment in national defense, thereby expanding and reproducing national power

[1884] Especially for us, facing a military standoff with North Korea, stability and peace, supported by a strong national defense, are essential conditions for economic development

[1885] Furthermore, considering the strategic environment we face and the close correlation between security and the economy, including our high level of external dependence, it is crucial to secure an appropriate level of military power commensurate with the world's 12th-largest economy

[1886] However, as of 2002, Korea's per capita defense spending ranked only 29th, and its defense budget to-GDP ratio is lower than that of other conflict-ridden and confrontational countries, such as Israel

[1887] To ensure the nation's survival and prosperity in an uncertain future security environment, active investment in national defense is essential

[1888] The 2004 defense budget was 2.8% of GDP, a 0.1 percentage point increase from

[1889] This is significant in that it marks the beginning of an upward trend in defense spending, a trend that has persisted for the past two decades

[1890] However, considering the comprehensive requirements for securing self-defense capabilities by sector and project, it is believed that defense spending should be allocated at a stable level of 3% or more of gross domestic product (GDP) in the mid- to long-term

[1940] Strengthening Eradication of Corruption, Bribery, and Irregularities Despite the efforts of past administrations to eradicate corruption, the public still perceives corruption as a serious problem in our society

[1943] To meet this government's commitment to eradicating corruption and fostering a culture of integrity in the military, the Ministry of National Defense has launched a large-scale anti-corruption and integrity campaign, as outlined below

[1944] First, on May 19, 2003, the Ministry of National Defense enacted and implemented the "Code of Conduct for Maintaining Integrity among Civil Servants of the Ministry of National Defense," marking a turning point by dismantling existing, unreasonable practices such as accepting bribes, gifts, entertainment, and hospitality

Military Judicial System Improvement Background and Progress In line with the launch of the Participatory Government, our military embarked on a comprehensive reform effort aimed at establishing a military judicial system that harmonizes judicial independence with the unique characteristics of military organizations

[2031] To this end, the Ministry of National Defense actively participated in the discussions on military judicial system reform by the Judicial Reform Committee under the Supreme Court, based on its own system improvement plan prepared in July

[2032] Through continuous consultation and debate within and outside the military, the Ministry developed measures to further strengthen the independence and fairness of military trials, the independence and expertise of military prosecutors, and the legitimacy of the disciplinary detention system

[2033] Legislative procedures are underway, with implementation targeted for

[2034] Key Improvements to the Military Judicial System Strengthening the Independence and Fairness of Military Trials Regarding the existing military tribunal system and operation, concerns have been raised about the potential undermining of judicial independence by unit commanders, the decline in the expertise of military judges, and the inefficiency of personnel management

[2035] To address these issues, a "judges' group" system was introduced, selecting military judges from among outstanding military judge advocates with a certain level of experience and integrating their affiliations into the Ministry of National Defense

[2036] This system enabled regional circuit trials

[2037] Furthermore, the peacetime operation of the judge system and the jurisdictional officer confirmation system, which had been criticized for violating the constitutional right to a trial by a judge and for violating fairness through arbitrary exercise of the right to reduce sentences, was discontinued, laying the institutional foundation for establishing the independence and authority of military trials

[2038] Strengthening the Independence and Expertise of the Military Prosecution Service To strengthen the independence of the military prosecution service, the military investigative and prosecutorial body, discussions are underway on two options: maintaining the current military prosecution service organizational structure while removing the specific command and supervision authority of unit commanders over the military prosecution service, or placing the military prosecution service under the Ministry of National Defense to strengthen its independence

[2039] Furthermore, discussions are underway to strengthen the efficiency of the investigative system by granting the military prosecutors the authority to direct investigations of specific cases over the military judicial police

[2040] Strengthening the Constitutionality of the Disciplinary Detention System Regarding disciplinary detention orders that involve personal detention, the legality and fairness of the detention system have been strengthened by introducing a system for military judge advocates to review the legality of disciplinary detention decisions and a system to suspend execution upon appeal

[2041] Meanwhile, reforms are also being pursued, including improvements to the personnel and human resources system to ensure the expertise of military judge advocates and improvements to the military penal system to strengthen the protection of the human rights of military prisoners

[2042] Reorganization of the Active Duty Force at the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters and Restructuring of the Military. Restructuring the Active Duty Forces of the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters (Civilianization

[2043] Civilianization refers to the institutionalization of civilian control, meaning that a group of politicians, including a civilian president and a civilian Minister of Defense, legally elected by the people, command and control the military

[2044] In other words, a group of civilian experts determines major national defense policies and guarantees the use of military force based on the nation's political and diplomatic policy decisions

[2045] The civilianization trend at the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters is a global trend

[2046] Representative countries of this civilianization include the United States, where the Ministry of National Defense's Military Commanders' Conference is comprised primarily of civilians specializing in security, and military personnel perform most of their duties within the Joint Chiefs of Staff's military command system

[2047] Within this environment, numerous security and defense-related research institutes operate in the Washington, D.C. area, where the Ministry of National Defense is located

[2048] Civilian professors are frequently outsourced to work in the defense field for an appropriate period of time before returning to their academic careers

[2049] The Ministry of National Defense believes that, as democracy has developed in Korea, the standards that the people and the government demand from the military have also significantly increased

[2050] The current climate is ripe for civilian elites to control the military, fostering the overall development of the national defense sector

[2051] Furthermore, if the Minister of National Defense's staff is comprised primarily of active-duty military personnel, it will be difficult to maintain a neutral perspective and balance in policy decision-making and implementation, and to escape a military-centric mindset

[2052] Therefore, civilianization is deemed essential to utilize talented individuals and lead the field military

[2053] Currently, the majority of senior positions at the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters are filled by active-duty military personnel and reservists with less than five years of service

[2054] The Policy Office and Acquisition Office are primarily comprised of military personnel, while the Planning and Management Office and the Vice Minister's Office are comprised primarily of general civil servants

[2055] Consequently, the level of civilianization and the system for efficient civilian control are considered immature

[2056] Therefore, to improve the civilian control environment, the Ministry of National Defense plans to gradually expand civilian positions at the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters in the mid- to long-term while optimizing military positions, focusing on essential positions

[2057] However, the core of civilianization is not simply the replacement of civilians

[2058] Rather than increasing the utilization rate, the policy aims to cultivate and appropriately utilize experts in military policy and military management while simultaneously enhancing the efficiency of comprehensive political and military work

[2059] Section 2 Status of Progress by Sector The goal is to achieve harmony in decision-making processes and organizational operations

[2060] The Ministry of National Defense will pursue the civilianization of the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters, guaranteeing the division of roles and authority between the Ministry of National Defense and the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and strengthening the Joint Chiefs of Staff's functions

[2061] Furthermore, by having the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, as the representative of the military, attend National Security Council (NSC) Standing Committee meetings and other meetings, the Ministry will create an environment where military opinions can be expressed in the decision-making process for government and defense policies

[2062] Signing Ceremony for Civilian-Military Military Studies Development Cooperation Moreover, to secure civilian military experts, it is crucial to establish and expand an educational system in related fields, such as by establishing military studies degree programs at general universities, to continuously cultivate excellent resources and supplement the military expertise of public officials

[2063] This is necessary

[2064] Therefore, the Ministry of National Defense is actively recruiting and training external experts, such as those who passed the civil service examination and former reserve forces, and having them lead the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters, enabling them to address both political and military issues
