[2096] Since taking office, Minister of National Defense Yoon Kwang-woong has consistently emphasized the implementation of "a defense that is with the people, a robust defense" through defense operations based on a new paradigm

[2097] This new defense paradigm requires the development of a civilian control system, the construction of military capabilities commensurate with national power, the maximization of integrated capabilities, and the establishment of a trustworthy military

[2098] The Need for a New Defense Paradigm This stems from the recognition that existing defense operations methods can no longer proactively respond to the rapidly changing security environment and defense conditions

[2099] Over the past half-century, our national defense has gradually developed under the special circumstances of confrontation with North Korea

[2100] However, to proactively respond to the rapidly evolving domestic and international security environment, a shift in the perceptions of those involved in the defense sector is necessary

[2101] This was urgently needed

[2102] That is, when assessing our current defense conditions and coordinates, we find ourselves in a dual situation of inter-Korean military confrontation and reconciliation and cooperation, and in a transitional security environment where the USFK is being realigned in accordance with the US's global defense posture review (Global Posture

[2103] Establishing a direction for military force development in line with the changing strategic environment and achieving cooperative self-reliant national defense are more urgent than ever

[2104] Today's security concept is evolving into a comprehensive concept encompassing politics, economy, society, and culture

[2105] Therefore, a bold shift to a paradigm at the national grand strategy level is necessary, ensuring that defense policies and strategies are formulated to implement the nation's security policies and strategies, and that military force development is pursued with consideration for national power and national status

[2106] Section 3 Future Defense Reform Directions Defense White Paper 207 Chapter 5 Defense Reform for the Future 208 2004 Defense White Paper Defense Reform Directions Based on a New Defense Paradigm A. Developing a Civilian Control System The Ministry of National Defense Headquarters, under the principle of civilian control, effectively manages, controls, and supports the military, which represents the government and the people

[2107] It implements and supports government policies and national strategies at the military level

[2108] By achieving a balance and harmony between the specialties and expertise of civilian officials and active-duty soldiers, it achieves a multiplier effect in national defense operations

[2109] Civilian control of the military must be developed into a system that manages and controls the military while recognizing the Ministry of National Defense's status and position at a national and governmental level

[2110] Furthermore, the role of professional personnel with a comprehensive and integrated perspective while understanding the military's unique characteristics must be emphasized

[2111] To this end, the concept of civilian control of the military must be established and developed, while simultaneously reviewing ways to supplement the functions of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and each service branch in accordance with the reorganization of the active-duty force composition of the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters

[2112] Personnel policies, such as promotions and positions, must be developed to minimize military-centric thinking and planning

[2113] At the same time, measures must be sought to effectively utilize the pool of military professionals already trained and utilized

[2114] Measures must be established to cultivate and secure specialized personnel

[2115] While strengthening self-defense capabilities to proactively respond to security threats, the national strategy should comprehensively consider economic power, international standing, and changes in the ROK-US alliance

[2116] Furthermore, cooperative self-defense based on a strategic concept should be promoted, allowing the ROK military to expand its leading role

[2117] Military power should be built to achieve national and military strategic goals

[2118] Furthermore, since defense funding stems from overall national power, including economic strength, the defense budget for military force construction and defense operations should be raised within the scope of national and military strategic concepts and available resources

[2119] Therefore, building military power is essential for achieving independent war deterrence

[2120] While prioritizing securing capabilities is crucial, each military branch and function should prioritize the development of one or two key forces to prepare for future, unspecified threats

[2121] To achieve this, intelligence and early warning capabilities should be secured to quickly expand independent surveillance, reconnaissance, command, control, and communications systems

[2122] Furthermore, bearing in mind that the nature of modern warfare has shifted from the "hearing war" of the past to a "seeing war," a battlefield management system capable of integrated real-time combat capabilities, including detection (sensor), decision-making (C4I), and strike (shooter), should be established

[2123] Furthermore, to secure precision strike capabilities against strategic targets in deep areas, South Korea should prioritize responding to North Korea's weapons of mass destruction (WMD) through grand strategic cooperation between South Korea and the United States and through international control systems

[2124] However, it should also secure the means to strike and neutralize them in the event of an emergency, as well as precision-guided weapons

[2125] Furthermore, it should reinforce its counterfirepower capabilities and long-range precision strike capabilities to overcome its firepower disadvantage against North Korea

[2126] Furthermore, it should secure forces capable of achieving air and maritime superiority at an early stage, thereby securing a war deterrent within the next decade

[2127] To meet the growing demand for UN peacekeeping operations (PKO), South Korea should actively participate in the UN standing system, including organizing an appropriately sized permanent overseas force and maintaining a standby posture

[2128] To ensure this, it should proactively reorganize relevant laws and institutions

[2129] Ensuring Maximized Unified Forces While reducing external dependence and overcoming functional imbalances in the construction, management, and operation of national defense capabilities, we will foster conditions for unified force deployment tailored to Korean characteristics and effectively prepare for future warfare

[2130] With the development of the national economy, the capabilities of the ROK military have steadily grown

[2131] The recent realignment of USFK provides an opportunity to expand the ROK military's role in ensuring our security

[2132] Through proactive restructuring and defense reform, our military must adapt to future warfare and transform into an information and science technology force capable of ensuring unified force deployment

[2133] To achieve this, we must establish a war-fighting system centered on the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), establish legal and institutional mechanisms to ensure balanced development across the Army, Navy, and Air Force, and transform the current force-intensive structure into a more efficient, elite, and technology-intensive one

[2134] To establish a JCS-centered war-fighting system, the JCS' independent war planning and operational execution functions and organizations must be strengthened, and the transfer of some functions of the Ministry of National Defense Headquarters linked to military command to the JCS should be considered

[2135] Furthermore, we must strengthen the organization to coordinate ROK-US command relations and acquire advanced military systems through the ROK-US Combined Forces Command (CFC) to continuously cultivate and secure a talented workforce

[2136] To establish institutional mechanisms to ensure the balanced development of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, we must establish concepts such as basic guidelines and direction for the balanced development of the three services

[2137] We must also review balanced personnel allocation and rotational appointment systems for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, national service, and joint units, and establish legal and institutional mechanisms, such as allocating necessary personnel to the Ministry of National Defense

[2138] Furthermore, we must review the investment budget system and strengthen analysis and evaluation functions to ensure the balanced distribution of defense resources, joint force building, and prevent redundant investments within each service

[2139] Establishing a Trustworthy Military We must foster a desirable military culture and service conditions, actively respond to the comprehensive security concept and the demands of civil society, and realize a national defense that serves the people

[2140] This will establish an image of the ROK military that secures public trust and support

[2141] Even a powerful military armed with cutting-edge weapons and equipment cannot achieve victory without the trust and support of the people

[2142] To establish a military trusted by the public, the military must develop and establish a desirable military culture through internal reform and enhance the leadership's command capabilities based on democracy and civilian control

[2143] Furthermore, while improving soldier morale, welfare, and service conditions, it must also implement an "open defense" that guarantees public participation, openness, and transparency

[2144] At the same time, it must practice "defense for the people" to protect the safety and interests of the people

[2145] To enhance the openness and transparency of national defense through "open defense," it is necessary to enhance the fairness of military administration and enhance customer orientation

[2146] It is necessary to proactively disclose defense administrative information, including current defense issues and matters of public interest, before the public demands them

[2147] Furthermore, it is necessary to expand the participation of civilian experts in the development of defense policy, thereby gathering diverse opinions from all walks of life

[2148] National Defense for the People" aims to more actively protect and promote the safety and interests of the people by establishing a system from peacetime to actively participate in national disaster management and support, and actively engaging in public support activities to redouble efforts to guarantee the people's property rights

[2149] Section 3 Future Directions for Defense Reform

[2208] In the era of "National Defense with the People," defense policies must be established and implemented transparently, and this process must be communicated truthfully to the public

[2209] To this end, our military believes that public participation and interest in defense policy are paramount, and has established and implemented a system to enable civilian experts from various fields to participate in the defense policy decision-making process

[2210] A. Defense Policy Advisory Committee

[2211] Since 1981, the Ministry of National Defense has operated the "National Defense Policy Advisory Committee," comprised of knowledgeable and experienced civilian experts from various fields, including academia and the media

[2212] The committee provides advice on national defense affairs and promotes mutual understanding and consensus between the civilian and military

[2213] The Defense Policy Advisory Committee, chaired by the Minister of National Defense, holds a plenary session once a year and subcommittee meetings at least once a quarter

[2214] The composition of advisory members for each of the 13 subcommittees is shown in Figure

[2215] Policy Office Planning and Management Office Deputy Minister's Office Acquisition Office Joint Chiefs of Staff Policy, International, Public Relations, and Education Planning, Cooperation, Public Information, Budget Legal Affairs Personnel Management Research Information Mobilization, Logistics, Facilities, Acquisition Development, System 2 3 In response to government policies aimed at expanding women's social participation, the Ministry of National Defense currently has 10 female advisory members, organized by field, as of

[2216] Considering the characteristics of each subcommittee, the committee plans to gradually increase the proportion of female members

[2217] Furthermore, a number of local government officials and members of civic groups are appointed as advisory members

[2218] We are striving to reflect diverse opinions from all walks of life in policymaking by appointing experts

[2219] In the past, private sector experts' participation in defense policy was achieved indirectly, through surveys, research results, and seminars

[2220] However, since 1998, private sector experts have been included as members of various policy review committees, allowing them to directly participate in policymaking and decision-making processes

[2221] To further promote this, the Ministry of National Defense developed the "Defense Reform Promotion Committee" into the "Defense Research Committee" in 2003 and appointed private sector experts and retired military experts as advisory committee members

[2222] Furthermore, to encourage private sector scholars to maintain an ongoing interest in defense issues, the ministry supports the hosting of defense-related academic seminars in the private sector, utilizing the opinions of private sector experts as valuable reference material for policy review and decision-making in related fields

[2223] Furthermore, research on defense issues previously conducted by the Korea Institute for Defense Analyses (KIDA) has been transferred to the private sector

[2224] By expanding its role as a research institute, it is gathering diverse opinions from civilian experts and utilizing them in policy development

[2225] Section 1: "Implementing an Open Defense" Chapter 6: Defense with the People Section 2: Implementing a National Defense for the People To implement a national defense for the people, the Ministry of National Defense is prioritizing groundbreaking improvements to military service administration that can foster public participation and interest

[2226] To foster an atmosphere where individuals voluntarily fulfill their military service obligations, it is introducing and implementing various systems to enhance the fairness and transparency of military service dispositions and expanding the system that allows individuals to choose their enlistment date and unit

[2227] It is actively practicing environmentally friendly military operations, such as preserving the environment of military bases and promoting local cleanup activities to prevent inconvenience to the public

[2228] It is also developing measures to mitigate noise from military airfields and firing ranges, which the public finds objectionable, and revising regulations on military facility protection zones to protect the public's property rights

[2229] Furthermore, it is protecting the public's property rights by addressing typhoons, In times of natural disasters, such as heavy snowfall, the military deploys troops and equipment to address the needs of the public

[2230] Improving Military Service Administration National security can be strengthened when military service is recognized as both a duty and an honor for citizens

[2231] The Ministry of National Defense is establishing a sound military service culture through improvements in military service administration

[2232] A. Continuous Innovation for a Healthy Military Service Culture Enhancing Fairness and Transparency in Military Service Dispositions Operating the Central Physical Examination Center for a Two tiered System for Military Service Exemption Decisions The Military Manpower Administration established and operates the Central Physical Examination Center in 2002 to address the fairness issues surrounding exemptions from military service (physical grades 5 and 6) based on the sole judgment of a conscription doctor, and to address the inconveniences faced by conscripts due to requests for detailed examinations from military hospitals

[2233] The Central Physical Examination Center, an independent, specialized agency for physical grade determinations, has been subdivided into 15 specialized fields

[2234] Dedicated Doctors Section 2: Implementing National Defense for the People A total of 22 doctors are working in this department

[2235] Furthermore, to prevent external requests or pressure related to physical examinations and ensure more precise examinations, multiple dedicated doctors are assigned to seven departments, including internal medicine, which have a high number of examinees

[2236] Decisions are made through consensus

[2237] Furthermore, state-of-the-art medical equipment, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), is being installed to ensure more accurate physical grade determinations

[2238] However, to address the inconvenience of secondary examinations for physical grades 5 and 6, physical grades for obvious conditions or conditions requiring guardian supervision are determined immediately by unanimous agreement of the Regional Military Manpower Administration Physical Grade Decision Review Committees, as before

[2239] MRI: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Magnetic Resonance Imaging Opening of the Central Physical Examination Center February 1, 2002 ㅇ Opening of the Central Physical Examination Center Also, to address the inconvenience of public complaints related to the implementation of the Central Physical Examination To resolve this issue, a physical examination reservation system has been implemented, allowing individuals to select their preferred examination date within a two-month period

[2240] Notably, since September 2003, the central physical examination process has been fully computerized and linked to the conscription examination systems of regional military manpower offices

[2241] This allows for real-time sharing of physical examination data and allows for organic processing of physical examination work with regional offices

[2242] Operation of the Physical Grade Determination Review Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Committee”) To prevent various irregularities in the physical grade determination process and ensure fair and transparent determination, the Military Service Act established the basis for the establishment of a committee related to fair physical examinations on February

[2243] The Military Manpower Administration has established and operates a "Military Manpower Administration Committee," a "Central Committee" at the Central Physical Examination Center, and a "Local Committee" at each regional military manpower office

[2244] The "Military Manpower Administration Committee" handles matters related to physical examinations and the physical grade determination system, while the "Central Committee" handles matters related to individuals whose physical grades are difficult to determine based on the results of the central physical examination

[2245] The "Local Committee" deliberates on those who have raised objections to physical grade assessments, such as those who are eligible for physical grades 5-6 according to the results of the local Military Manpower Administration's conscription physical examination but have been excluded from the central physical examination due to a clear medical condition (119 diseases under the examination regulations, including the conscription physical examination), and those who have raised objections

[2246] Notably, since 2003, those with physical grades 4-6 have been additionally included in the review as priority management targets

[2247] Decisions on physical grades are made by the "Local Committee," comprised of conscription officers, senior conscription doctors, and relevant departments

[2248] Defense White Paper 223 Chapter 6: National Defense with the People 224 2004 Defense White Paper Conscription doctors, and external members appointed by the head of the local Military Manpower Administration (Citizens' Participation Committee for Military Administration Development, members of non-profit organizations such as the Anti-Corruption People's Solidarity for Participatory Democracy, etc

[2249] Decisions are made by unanimous agreement

[2250] If not, the Central Physical Examination Center will be requested to conduct a detailed examination

[2251] The Central Committee first determines the physical grade by unanimous agreement at a review committee of at least seven members, including the Central Physical Examination Center Director, the Operations Officer, the Chief Conscription Doctor, the relevant department conscription doctor, and the conscription doctor from the Diagnostic Radiology Department

[2252] If agreement cannot be reached, the two physical grades with the most opinions will be determined by a second review committee comprised of all conscription doctors at the Central Physical Examination Center

[2253] The grade that receives the majority vote will be determined as the physical grade

[2254] In the event of a tie, the chairperson will decide

[2255] Selection and Management of Priority Management Diseases In 2003, some conscripts were found to be abusing tattoos, hyperhidrosis surgery, and other methods to evade active duty

[2256] To prevent this, 16 diseases with the potential for physical damage and fraud were selected as priority management diseases

[2257] The priority management diseases are physical grades

[2258] Subjects are referred to the "Local Committee" to determine their physical grade

[2259] If intentional conduct is determined, a report of the disease or mental or physical disability is obtained, and a written opinion from a conscription doctor is attached

[2260] A request for investigation is made to the chief of the police station

[2261] The situation regarding conscription physical examinations, including the monthly increase or decrease in the number of supplementary service members or exemptions, is closely analyzed

[2262] If any issues are determined, immediate action is taken

[2263] The Honorary Ombudsman for Conscription Examinations actively listens to complaints and grievances from subjects of physical examinations and their families, and is appointed as an Honorary Ombudsman

[2264] Members of the Citizens' Participation Committee for Military Administration Development and external members of civic groups such as the Anti-Corruption Citizens' Coalition and People's Solidarity for Participatory Democracy are appointed as Honorary Ombudsmen

[2265] Progress is being made to the conscription doctor

[2266] Implementation of a system to exclude relatives from physical examinations

[2267] The conscription doctor, who is the judge of physical grade, is responsible for the conscription doctor's role

[2268] To eliminate the potential for unfair physical grade assessments due to requests from relatives and in-laws and to dispel negative public perceptions, a physical examination exclusion system has been in place since 2004 for relatives and in-laws of conscription doctors

[2269] Eligible for exclusion are blood relatives within the 8th degree of kinship and relatives within the 4th degree of kinship

[2270] If the conscription doctor himself determines a physical grade of 4-6, the local office requests a central physical examination

[2271] If a conscription doctor affiliated with the Central Physical Examination Center determines a physical grade, the request is referred to the Central Committee, which then determines the physical grade

[2273] To ensure fair and efficient implementation, selection criteria for designated alternative service providers are being strengthened, service discipline is being established, and ongoing training is being provided

[2284] Strengthening Management of Military Service Resources Residing and Moving Abroad Recently, cases of overseas stays being used as a means of military service evasion have become a social issue

[2285] Accordingly, to efficiently manage military service resources, we are ensuring maximum convenience for those who actually live abroad, while strengthening management of those who attempt to evade military service by abusing the system

[2286] Accordingly, even if a person has received exemption or postponement of military service for reasons such as obtaining permanent residency for the entire family, they must remain in Korea for more than one year or be in a continuous employment relationship

[2287] Those who receive a salary or other compensation, or who provide other personal services and earn more than 10 million won annually, and who have stayed in Korea for more than 60 days are subject to cancellation of overseas travel permits and mandatory military service

[2288] Military Service Dispositions for Permanent Residents with Full Family Members. Currently, those who obtained permanent residency with their family members abroad are exempt from military service without undergoing a physical examination

[2289] However, this is often mistaken for permanent exemption, resulting in innocent victims

[2290] Therefore, the term "military service exemption" has been changed to "military service postponement" to prevent innocent victims and address negative public opinion regarding military service exemption

[2291] Allowed Period of Domestic Stay While military service obligations are imposed on individuals residing overseas who remain in Korea for more than one year, many remain in Korea for extended periods, repeatedly departing and returning

[2292] However, the period of stay for those who re-enter the country within six months is now counted, resulting in innocent victims

[2293] Consequently, the allowable period of domestic stay will be shortened from one year to a total of six months or more per year

[2363] Therefore, the military is continuously developing a public-private-military cooperation system

[2366] In addition, the "Military Environmental Conservation Conference," attended by environmental experts, environmental practitioners, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs), is held annually to identify and analyze environmental issues within the military and develop improvement measures

[2424] Institutional Improvement and Deregulation Related to Military Facility Protection Zones To ensure the protection of critical military facilities and the smooth conduct of military operations, the ROK military has enacted laws related to the protection of military facilities (bases), including the "Military Facility Protection Act," the "Naval Base Act," and the "Air Base Act

[2425] Based on these laws, approximately 3.21 billion pyeong of land has been designated and managed as military facility (base) protection zones in border areas and areas surrounding major military facilities

[2426] However, as a large portion of the national land has been designated as military facility (base) protection zones, this has limited efficient land use and caused inconvenience to residents

[2427] Therefore, we are pursuing institutional improvement and deregulation related to military facility (base) protection zones

[2428] Legislative Revisions and System Improvements Various laws and regulations related to military facility (base) protection zones have been revised several times since their enactment in

[2431] Previously, no new construction or expansion of housing was permitted within the ammunition depot protection area

[2432] However, this revision allows for relocation of buildings if demolition is unavoidable due to public projects such as railways and roads

[2433] The base protection area, previously set at 5km from the outer boundary of an air base, was reduced to 2km

[2434] Within the specified building height range within the military facility protection area, consultation work was delegated to administrative agencies to simplify military consultation procedures

[2444] Section 2: Implementing National Defense for the People Chapter 6: National Defense with the People B. Public Support Activities in the Event of Disasters Recently, due to global warming and other climate change, large-scale natural disasters such as typhoons, floods, and heavy snowfalls have been on the rise

[2445] There is growing concern that these disaster conditions will worsen in the future

[2446] However, social development driven by economic growth has also increased public demand for disaster-free living

[2447] To meet the public's demand for safety, the participatory government enacted and promulgated the "Basic Act on Disaster and Safety Management" (March 1, 2004) and established the National Emergency Management Agency (June 1, 2004), comprehensively reorganizing the government's disaster management system

[2448] The Ministry of National Defense also established the Disaster Management Support Division (August 14, 2004) and, under a comprehensive security concept, is making every effort to provide prevention and recovery support to protect the lives and property of the public from not only traditional military threats but also various disasters. Establishing a New Paradigm for National Defense Disaster Management Policy It is well known that our military has provided dedicated public support whenever national disasters occur, such as Typhoon Rusa in 2002, Typhoon Maemi in 2003, and the heavy snowfall in the central region in

[2449] Despite this, disaster management has been relatively neglected in the traditional security concept, which mandates protecting the lives and property of citizens and defending the nation from external invasion

[2450] Going forward, the Ministry of National Defense has decided to explore a more active role for the military in national disaster management

[2451] First, under a comprehensive security concept, the military will be required to perform public support in the event of a national disaster as its primary mission

[2452] This will be reflected in various documents, including the Basic Defense Policy and the National Defense White Paper

[2453] To support this, a Disaster Management Support Division will be established at Army Headquarters by 2005, and team-level organizations will be established at Navy and Air Force Headquarters

[2454] Repair of greenhouses during heavy snowfall in March Emergency relief supplies support The Ministry of National Defense also shared information on available disaster management assets between the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's National Emergency Management Agency and the military, and institutionalized a cooperative system by signing support agreements between the Ministry of National Defense and the National Emergency Management Agency, and between local military units and local governments

[2455] Defense White Paper It was decided

[2456] Furthermore, for 11 types of natural and man-made disasters, including typhoons and tsunamis, and 8 types of national infrastructure protection, a detailed practical manual for immediate use in the event of a disaster will be developed in conjunction with the NSC Crisis Management Standard Manual

[2457] This manual will be distributed and utilized throughout the military

[2458] Furthermore, for the military's proactive support of the public in the event of a disaster, a basic understanding of all commanders and soldiers is crucial

[2459] Therefore, disaster management courses will be established at all levels of military institutions, including the National Defense University, and expert lectures will be organized

[2460] Furthermore, commissioned training for emergency rescue workers, disaster management personnel, and instructors will be expanded annually to firefighting academies, the National 119 Rescue Team, civilian universities, and disaster management research centers

[2461] This new paradigm for national defense disaster management policy will enhance public trust as the military of the people, ultimately contributing significantly to the strengthening of the military's combat readiness and enhanced capabilities

[2606] ※ November 28, 2000 ~, South Korea's Chief Representative for the Working-Level Military Talks: Army Brigadier General Kim Kyung-duk, Deputy Director of Arms Control October 25, 2002 ~, South Korea's Chief Representative for the Working-Level Military Talks: Army Colonel Moon Seong-mook, Director of the Ministry of National Defense's Talk Operations Task Force May 26, 2004 ~, South Korea's Chief Representative for the General-Level Military Talks: Navy Brigadier General Park Jeong-hwa, Deputy Director of Operational Planning, Joint Chiefs of Staff 1st Joint Press Release on the Inter-Korean Defense Ministers' Meeting

[2607] To ensure the military implementation of the June 15th Inter-Korean Joint Declaration adopted at the historic inter-Korean summit, talks between the Minister of National Defense of the Republic of Korea and the Minister of the People's Armed Forces of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea were held on Jeju Island in the South from September 25th to 26th

[2608] The talks were attended by five representatives from the South, led by Minister of National Defense Cho Sung-tae, and five representatives from the North, led by Vice Marshal Kim Il-chol, Minister of the People's Armed Forces of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea

[2609] During the talks, both sides shared the view that appropriate military measures were required amid the full-scale implementation of the June 15th Inter-Korean Joint Declaration and agreed on the following issues

[2610] The two sides agreed that the leaders of the South and the North should make their utmost efforts to implement the June 15th Inter-Korean Joint Declaration and actively cooperate to resolve military issues arising from ensuring civilian travel, exchange, and cooperation

[2611] Both sides shared the understanding that easing military tensions, establishing a permanent and solid peace on the Korean Peninsula, and eliminating the danger of war are urgent issues, and agreed to work together to achieve this

[2612] Both sides agreed to permit the entry of personnel, vehicles, and equipment into each side's Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) for the urgent task of constructing railways and roads connecting the South and the North, and to guarantee their safety

[2613] Working-level officials from both sides agreed to meet in early October to discuss specific details

[2614] The issue of opening the Military Demarcation Line and the DMZ along the railways and roads connecting the South and the North and establishing areas under the jurisdiction of the South and the North will be addressed based on the Armistice Agreement

[2615] Both sides agreed to hold the second round of talks in the North in mid-November

[2690] The meeting was led by Minister of National Defense Cho Young-gil of the Republic of Korea and Secretary of Defense Donald Rumsfeld of the United States, and was attended by senior defense and foreign affairs officials from both countries

[2691] Prior to the meeting On November 15, 2003, the ROK and U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Kim Jong-hwan and General Richard Myers, presided over the 25th ROK-U.S. Military Committee Meeting

[2692] Secretary Rumsfeld expressed appreciation for President Roh Moo-hyun's decision to deploy additional troops to Iraq and provide $260 million in reconstruction funding from 2003 to

[2693] Secretary Rumsfeld pledged to work closely with the ROK to ensure a smooth and timely deployment, particularly regarding information sharing and logistics planning

[2694] Secretary Rumsfeld praised the efforts of ROK troops already deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, noting that they have demonstrated world-class military capabilities

[2695] The Secretary and the Minister agreed on the need to support the Iraqi and Afghan people in rebuilding their countries and in establishing stable, democratic institutions capable of preventing attacks and eliminating terrorism

[2696] The Minister agreed that the ROK's additional deployment of troops to Iraq would further strengthen the ROK-U.S. alliance

[2697] They assessed that this would serve as an opportunity to strengthen Korea's alliance with the United States and elevate Korea's status in the international community

[2699] The two Ministers noted the significance of the 50th anniversary of the ROK-U.S. Mutual Defense Treaty, which was signed on October 1, 1953, and praised the achievements of the ROK-U.S. Alliance over the past half-century

[2700] They also commended the efforts of ROK and U.S. service members to ensure peace and prosperity in the region

[2701] The Ministers expressed their strong belief that the ROK-U.S. partnership forms the foundation of both countries' interests and pledged to continue efforts to strengthen and enhance the alliance for the future

[2702] The Ministers expressed satisfaction with the results to date of the Future ROK-U.S. Alliance Policy Initiative Consultations, held in 2003 and scheduled to continue in

[2703] The Minister and the Secretary reviewed the agreements on the relocation of USFK within Seoul, the enhancement of combined military capabilities, the transition of military missions, and the realignment of USFK

[2704] The two Ministers agreed that the full implementation of these initiatives will modernize and strengthen the ROK-US Alliance and make it more adaptable to the changing global security environment

[2705] In this regard, the Minister and the Secretary reaffirmed the continued importance of the strategic flexibility of USFK

[2706] Recalling the agreement between President Roh Moo-hyun and President Bush to relocate USFK from downtown Seoul at an early date, the Minister and the Secretary expressed regret that the ROK and the US failed to reach an agreement before this SCM

[2713] The Minister and the Secretary reaffirmed the principle of a two-phase relocation and integration of U.S. forces stationed in Korea into two areas south of the Han River

[2714] The Minister and the Secretary agreed that this realignment and integration of USFK will strengthen combined readiness, enhance force protection, promote efficient use and balanced development of the Republic of Korea's territory, and create an environment where USFK can continue to contribute to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula

[2715] The Minister and the Secretary emphasized that Phase 1 will commence as soon as possible and reaffirmed that the timing of Phase 2 realignment will be determined by the highest leaderships of the two countries, in accordance with the principles contained in the Joint Statements of the ROK-US Summits of May 14 and October

[2717] The Minister and the Secretary expressed grave concern that North Korea's self-acknowledged nuclear weapons development program threatens global and regional security and violates North Korea's commitment to the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula

[2718] The Minister and the Secretary emphasized that North Korea's efforts to develop weapons of mass destruction and long-range missiles, and the risks of exporting such weapons and related technologies, are a cause for grave concern for the alliance between the two countries and the international community

[2719] The Minister and the Secretary reaffirmed that North Korea's use of weapons of mass destruction would have serious consequences

[2720] The Minister and the Secretary urged North Korea to completely, verifiably, and irreversibly dismantle its nuclear weapons development program and to cease testing, developing, deploying, and exporting weapons of mass destruction, missiles, and related technologies

[2723] Secretary Rumsfeld said that under the Mutual Defense Treaty, They agreed on the need for the continued presence of US forces under the US defense commitment and nuclear umbrella for Korea, and that the ROK-US alliance will contribute to promoting peace and stability in Northeast Asia and the Asia-Pacific region as a whole
